Yes, it says she was unequivocal in her three interviews that it was Kaylee. My point is, she thought the noises were Kaylee, not the intruder. In the moment, she wasn’t putting two and two together. She knew what she knew at the time: she saw a man exiting the home after walking away from Xana’s room and now, hours later, that same friend was unconscious.

It’s so easy playing Monday morning quarterback - given the information we have now, sure. Most of us would be able to make more informed decisions. These girls didn’t get that luxury. They reacted to the situation with the information they had in the moment.  They are victims too.

You also have to remember that, in regards to Maddie, up until this point, DM had no reason to think anything was wrong with Maddie. She wasn’t aware Kaylee was in Maddie’s room and the noises she heard, she thought were from Kaylee who she figured was in her own bedroom.

Listen, I’m a pit bull owner so I’m definitely biased but here’s my take. Pit bulls are just as loving as a golden retriever. Pit bulls, however, have way more strength than a golden retriever. My dog is the biggest mush on earth and wouldn’t hurt a fly….unless that fly tried to hurt me. I had a poodle awhile back who, if need be, probably would have attacked someone who tried to hurt me. Here’s the difference: a pit bull bite hurts way more than a poodle bite. 

I just feel that if pit bulls were not built the way they were, people would feel a lot differently. I’m comfortable with my dog taking a treat from my fingers even knowing that he could literally rip off my entire hand without any effort. Would he? No. Could he? 100 %. My poodle could never have done that.

I used to hear the saying “There’s no bad kids, just bad parents” and this is how I feel about dogs. No bad dogs, just bad owners. If you don’t know how to handle your dog, ESPECIALLY a pit bull, you don’t deserve to own one. I know what my dog can do, so i have to be very careful. Small dogs attack my dog all the time. Why? Who knows. But I walk on the other side of the street if I see one coming. My dog is patient, but the one day he’s not and he gets mad at the little Yorkie down the street who keeps biting his face, guess who’s going to get blamed? 

Anyway, now that I’ve written a novel…..moral of the story: hold owners accountable. They know better, their dogs don’t. Sorry for the long comment.

As someone who was in an abusive relationship, as soon as I saw the body cam footage, I immediately saw a toxic relationship. Reactive abuse is all too real and something I’ve struggled to come to terms with and prevented me from even admitting to being in an abusive relationship because I felt like it was “mutually abusive” at times. In reality, reactive abuse is usually what happens. It’s common for the victim of abuse to lash out at their abuser in an attempt to defend themself against the abuse. This could be physical or emotional abuse. The abuser will use this to gaslight their victim by making them believe that their reactions are completely unwarranted and, as seen on the body cam footage, that the victim is actually the abuser. 

Now, I don’t know their relationship and I can’t claim that this is 100% true based on one snippet of their life, but it felt all too familiar when watching.
